speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain. To help me understand your condition, have you had any recent chest trauma, or are you taking any new medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome. The history of forceful vomiting, subsequent choking, and chest pain following alcohol consumption is classic for esophageal rupture. I am requesting a Chest_X-Ray and a CT scan of the chest with contrast to confirm the diagnosis.
